assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is detecting genuine-vs-manufactured hype and counting independent origins; content moderation and takedown policy are out of scope
per-platform engagement, search-trends, and content provenance metadata are available across five platforms
genuine hype requires at least N independent origins after provenance deduplication (scope finding FP7)
exclusions: content moderation, takedown, and enforcement policy
real-time streaming infrastructure and crawl execution internals

competency_questions.question: What is the expected organic engagement baseline and diffusion shape for a topic on a platform?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORGANIC_BASELINE sets expected engagement and DIFFUSION_CURVE the expected adoption shape

competency_questions.question: How is the expected adoption S-curve characterized and how is structural virality measured?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DIFFUSION_CURVE fits Bass p/q/m and STRUCTURAL_VIRALITY measures the cascade tree

competency_questions.question: What semi-independent demand signals corroborate engagement and how are platforms reconciled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEARCH_INTEREST supplies a pull signal and CROSS_PLATFORM_RECONCILE aligns platform signals

competency_questions.question: How is a burst distinguished from expected variation and validated against labeled episodes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANOMALY_DETECTION flags significant bursts and BASELINE_BACKTEST validates separation

competency_questions.question: How are cross-posts and reposts collapsed to seeds and reconciled before counting origins?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROVENANCE_CLUSTERING collapses reposts and CROSS_PLATFORM_RECONCILE aligns them

competency_questions.question: How are distinct independent origins counted and how is common-method non-independence handled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOURCE_INDEPENDENCE counts distinct origins and COMMON_METHOD_BIAS discounts shared-method sources

competency_questions.question: How is raw engagement discounted to adjusted hype using bot risk and saturation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RAW_VS_ADJUSTED_HYPE applies BOT_RISK_SCORING and SATURATION_ESTIMATE discounts

competency_questions.question: How does audience saturation affect the genuineness of late-stage engagement?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SATURATION_ESTIMATE estimates fraction of m reached and feeds RAW_VS_ADJUSTED_HYPE

competency_questions.question: How is the hype trajectory classified and broadcast distinguished from genuine virality?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HYPE_TRAJECTORY labels the phase and STRUCTURAL_VIRALITY separates broadcast from viral

competency_questions.question: How is manufactured hype adjudicated against genuine hype across multiple signals?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MANUFACTURED_HYPE fuses signals into a verdict gated by GENUINE_HYPE_THRESHOLD

competency_questions.question: Why does genuine hype require at least N independent origins after dedup, and who governs N?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GENUINE_HYPE_THRESHOLD enforces the >=N independence gate governed by THRESHOLD_GOVERNANCE

competency_questions.question: What does the final genuine-hype decision report contain and how is trajectory included?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DECISION_REPORT assembles the verdict, magnitude, and HYPE_TRAJECTORY phase

competency_questions.question: How are thresholds, N, and verdict evidence governed and made reproducible?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THRESHOLD_GOVERNANCE versions parameters and EVIDENCE_LEDGER records reproducible verdicts

competency_questions.question: How is the whole pipeline validated and reported so verdicts are auditable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BASELINE_BACKTEST calibrates and validates, EVIDENCE_LEDGER records, DECISION_REPORT reports

glossary.definition: the expected engagement a topic attracts under normal diffusion for a given platform, region, and category, used as the deviation reference
an adoption model with innovation coefficient p, imitation coefficient q, and market potential m yielding an S-shaped cumulative-adoption curve
the average shortest-path distance (Wiener index) of a diffusion tree, distinguishing broadcast from multi-generational spread
a causally and organizationally distinct source of a topic after provenance dedup and method-bias discounting
the single underlying artifact to which all its cross-posts, screenshots, and re-uploads are clustered
shared instrumentation or data-collection pipeline that makes nominally distinct sources non-independent
raw engagement discounted for bot risk and audience saturation to approximate genuine novel human attention
a hype event produced by seeding, astroturfing, or coordinated inauthentic behavior rather than organic demand
the policy that genuine hype requires at least N independent origins after deduplication, independent of volume

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for genuine-vs-manufactured hype and source-independence work units, grounded in diffusion modeling, structural-virality, source-independence intelligence analysis, and anomaly-detection literature; no supplied dataset
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Bass 1969 A New Product Growth Model for Consumer Durables (diffusion p/q/m); Berger & Milkman 2012 What Makes Online Content Viral (JMR); Heuer 1999 Psychology of Intelligence Analysis (source independence and corroboration); Goel, Anderson, Hofman & Watts 2016 The Structural Virality of Online Diffusion (Management Science); Chandola, Banerjee & Kumar 2009 Anomaly Detection: A Survey (ACM Computing Surveys)

nodes.definition: Estimate the expected engagement (views, reshares, comments) a topic should attract per platform, region, and content category under normal organic diffusion, to serve as the reference against which observed hype is judged.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: platform algorithm change, seasonality shift, or new region/category added to the baseline panel

pros.claim: A calibrated organic baseline turns 'this looks big' into a quantitative deviation, the prerequisite for any anomaly judgment
pros.example: a fashion reel at 40k views means little until the category baseline says median is 8k

cons.claim: Baselines drift silently when the platform changes ranking, making yesterday's 'normal' wrong today
cons.example: a feed-algorithm update doubles organic reach and inflates every deviation

failure_modes: baseline computed on a non-comparable audience (wrong region/category)
stale baseline from before an algorithm change
survivorship bias from only sampling already-viral items
acceptance_tests: baseline reproduces held-out organic items' engagement within its stated confidence interval
baseline panel covers every platform/region/category the verdict will be issued for
revisit_triggers: platform ranking algorithm changes
baseline residuals show systematic drift over weeks

nodes.definition: Fit the Bass diffusion model (innovation coefficient p, imitation coefficient q, market potential m) to a topic's cumulative adoption, characterizing the expected S-curve shape that genuine word-of-mouth spread produces.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: diffusion model family changes or p/q priors are recalibrated for a platform

pros.claim: The Bass model gives a principled expected adoption shape so deviations from genuine word-of-mouth become measurable, not eyeballed
pros.example: a genuine trend follows a smooth p+q*(N/m) hazard, not a vertical jump

cons.claim: Bass assumes a single homogeneous market and one initiating event, so multi-seed or networked spread fits poorly
cons.example: a meme reignited by three unrelated creators violates the single-market assumption

failure_modes: fitting Bass to a partial/early curve yields unstable q
forcing an S-curve onto genuinely networked structural-virality spread
ignoring repeat adoption inflates m
acceptance_tests: fitted curve reproduces the held-out tail of a known-organic trend within tolerance
p and q lie in plausible ranges seen for the platform
revisit_triggers: new platform with unknown p/q priors
structural-virality patterns recur that Bass cannot fit

nodes.definition: Track search-query interest (e.g., trends indices) for the topic as a semi-independent demand signal that, unlike platform engagement, reflects pull-driven attention and is less easily inflated by a single seeding campaign.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: search-trends provider methodology changes or query-mapping for the topic is revised

pros.claim: Search interest is a pull signal a push campaign cannot easily manufacture, so concordance with engagement is corroborating evidence of genuine demand
pros.example: a product whose hype rises but whose searches stay flat is likely push-only

cons.claim: Search indices are coarse, normalized, and sampled, and brand-name queries can be gamed by ad spend
cons.example: a paid search campaign lifts the trends curve without organic demand

failure_modes: mapping the wrong queries to the topic
treating a privacy-sampled index as exact counts
ignoring that searches lag virality by hours
acceptance_tests: search interest for a known-organic topic correlates positively with its independent-origin engagement
revisit_triggers: trends provider changes normalization
search-engagement correlation breaks for known cases

nodes.definition: Detect statistically significant bursts: flag windows where observed engagement deviates from the organic baseline and Bass-expected trajectory beyond a chosen threshold, distinguishing real surges from normal variation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: anomaly-detection method or significance threshold changes

pros.claim: Casting hype as anomaly detection against an expected model is a well-studied, falsifiable framing rather than ad hoc spike-spotting
pros.example: a 6-sigma residual over the Bass-expected window is an objective burst flag

cons.claim: Anomaly thresholds trade false positives against missed bursts, and bursty platforms have heavy-tailed normals
cons.example: a viral-but-organic Friday spike trips a Gaussian threshold tuned on weekdays

failure_modes: Gaussian thresholds on heavy-tailed engagement over-flag
change-point lag misses fast bursts
baseline error propagates into every anomaly score
acceptance_tests: on labeled organic surges, false-positive rate stays under the configured target
detected bursts align with known seeding events in the validation set
revisit_triggers: engagement distribution shifts to heavier tails
false-positive rate exceeds target on review

nodes.definition: Cluster content items that are cross-posts, screenshots, re-uploads, or quote-shares of the same underlying artifact so that one piece of content propagated across surfaces collapses to a single provenance seed.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: matching method (perceptual hash, near-dup text, watermark) changes or a new repost surface appears

pros.claim: Collapsing reposts to one seed prevents counting a single artifact's spread as many independent signals, the core deduplication step
pros.example: one screenshot reposted to five accounts is one seed, not five origins

cons.claim: Aggressive clustering can merge genuinely distinct independent creations of similar content into one seed
cons.example: two creators independently filming the same public event get wrongly merged

failure_modes: perceptual hash collisions merge distinct content
missed match leaves duplicates as fake independence
cropping/re-encoding defeats the matcher
acceptance_tests: known repost chains in the validation set collapse to one seed each
independently-created near-duplicates are not merged on the labeled set
revisit_triggers: a new repost/quote-share surface emerges
matcher precision or recall degrades on audit

nodes.definition: Reduce a set of platform signals to DISTINCT independent origins: after provenance clustering, determine how many causally and organizationally independent sources actually carry the topic, because multi-platform agreement can collapse to a single origin.

included: collapsing correlated platforms to shared origins

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: independence definition or origin-merging rules change

pros.claim: Heuer's intelligence principle that corroboration requires source independence directly applies: five platforms echoing one press release is one source, not five
pros.example: cross-platform agreement is discounted to its true independent-origin count

cons.claim: Independence is hard to observe; shared funding, coordinated networks, and syndication hide behind apparent diversity
cons.example: an astroturf network of 'independent' accounts shares one operator

failure_modes: treating correlated platforms as independent inflates corroboration
missing a shared operator behind diverse-looking accounts
syndicated wire content counted as many origins
acceptance_tests: five platforms tracing to one press release reduce to one independent origin on the labeled set
known astroturf networks collapse to their true operator count
revisit_triggers: evidence of coordinated/syndicated networks emerges
independence assumptions contradicted by provenance audit

nodes.definition: Account for common-method bias: sources sharing the same data-collection method, instrumentation, or platform pipeline are not truly independent even if nominally distinct, and their agreement must be discounted.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: shared-method taxonomy changes or a new common pipeline is identified

pros.claim: Naming common-method variance prevents mistaking shared-pipeline artifacts for independent corroboration, a known confound in survey and measurement science
pros.example: two 'independent' trackers both buying the same third-party panel are one method

cons.claim: Method correlation is partly latent and easy to under- or over-estimate, risking both inflated and deflated independence
cons.example: over-discounting punishes sources that merely use common best-practice tooling

failure_modes: ignoring shared third-party data panels
conflating method overlap with topical correlation
double-counting after both clustering and method discounting
acceptance_tests: sources sharing a single data panel are flagged as method-correlated on the labeled set
independence count after discounting does not double-penalize already-clustered seeds
revisit_triggers: a new shared data pipeline is discovered
method-correlation estimates contradicted by audit

nodes.definition: Score the share of engagement attributable to bots, sockpuppets, and coordinated inauthentic behavior on each origin, producing a per-signal bot-risk estimate used to discount raw hype.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bot-detection model or coordination heuristics change

pros.claim: A per-origin bot-risk score lets raw engagement be discounted by inauthenticity rather than trusted at face value
pros.example: an origin with 70% burst accounts created same-day is heavily discounted

cons.claim: Bot detection is adversarial and lags new evasion, so scores are systematically conservative and can be evaded
cons.example: a sophisticated farm with aged, warmed accounts evades behavioral signals

failure_modes: false-positive bot labels suppress genuine grassroots accounts
detector blind to a new automation pattern
coordination scored per-account misses network-level patterns
acceptance_tests: on labeled bot campaigns the bot-risk score exceeds the genuine-baseline score
grassroots known-organic origins are not flagged as high bot-risk
revisit_triggers: a new automation/evasion pattern appears
bot-risk scores diverge from labeled audits

nodes.definition: Estimate how saturated the addressable audience already is for the topic (fraction of market potential m already reached), since late-stage engagement on a saturated topic signals less genuine novel demand than early-stage growth.
inputs: fitted Bass m and cumulative adoption

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: market-potential m estimate or saturation model changes

pros.claim: Saturation context discounts plateau-phase engagement that looks large but represents recycled, not novel, attention
pros.example: 100k late reshares on a near-saturated topic add little genuine novelty

cons.claim: Market potential m is itself estimated and unstable, so the saturation fraction inherits that uncertainty
cons.example: an underestimated m makes a still-growing topic look prematurely saturated

failure_modes: using a stale m from before audience growth
confusing saturation with genuine fading
saturation discount applied twice with the curve fit
acceptance_tests: saturation estimate tracks the fitted curve's cumulative fraction on known trends
early-stage genuine growth is not over-discounted as saturated
revisit_triggers: market-potential m is revised
saturation estimates mismatch observed plateaus

nodes.definition: Compute adjusted hype by discounting raw engagement for bot risk and audience saturation, so the headline number reflects plausibly genuine human, novel attention rather than inflated or recycled volume.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: discounting formula or weighting of bot/saturation factors changes

pros.claim: Separating raw from adjusted hype makes the inflation explicit and auditable instead of buried in a single number
pros.example: raw 500k reshares at 60% bot-risk and high saturation yields ~120k adjusted

cons.claim: Multiplicative discounts can compound errors from two noisy estimators into a misleadingly precise adjusted figure
cons.example: small errors in bot and saturation each compound in the product

failure_modes: double-counting a discount already applied upstream
treating adjusted hype as exact rather than an interval
negative or clipped values from over-discounting
acceptance_tests: adjusted hype on labeled manufactured campaigns falls far below raw, while genuine campaigns stay close to raw
adjusted-hype confidence interval is reported, not just a point
revisit_triggers: discount weighting policy changes
adjusted-vs-raw gap behaves unexpectedly on audits

nodes.definition: Measure structural virality (the Goel et al. average-distance/Wiener-index of the diffusion tree) to distinguish a broadcast (one source to many) from genuine multi-generational person-to-person spread.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: structural-virality estimator or reshare-tree reconstruction method changes

pros.claim: Goel et al. show identical popularity can arise from a broadcast or true virality; structural virality tells them apart, which raw counts cannot
pros.example: a star-shaped tree from one influencer is broadcast, not grassroots virality

cons.claim: Reshare-tree reconstruction is noisy and platforms expose incomplete cascade data, biasing the structural-virality estimate
cons.example: missing parent edges flatten the tree toward apparent broadcast

failure_modes: incomplete cascade data biases the Wiener index
conflating high reach with high structural virality
tree reconstruction errors from missing edges
acceptance_tests: broadcast cascades score low structural virality and grassroots cascades score high on labeled trees
structural-virality estimate is stable under modest missing-edge rates
revisit_triggers: platform changes cascade-data availability
structural-virality estimates contradict known broadcast/viral labels

nodes.definition: Adjudicate whether a hype event is manufactured (seeded, astroturfed, or coordinated) versus genuine, by combining anomaly evidence, low independent-origin count, high bot-risk, broadcast structure, and absent search corroboration.

included: confidence and rationale on the verdict

inputs: anomaly, independence, bot, structural, and search signals

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: adjudication evidence weighting or manufactured-hype definition changes

pros.claim: A multi-signal adjudication is robust to any single gameable metric, since manufacturing must defeat baseline, independence, bot, structure, and search jointly
pros.example: a campaign can buy reshares but rarely also fakes independent origins and organic search

cons.claim: Fusing correlated signals risks overconfidence, and a determined operator can partially spoof several at once
cons.example: a well-funded campaign seeds genuine-looking micro-influencers across surfaces

failure_modes: over-weighting one signal makes the verdict gameable
correlated evidence treated as independent inflates confidence
verdict issued without recording which signals drove it
acceptance_tests: labeled astroturf campaigns are adjudicated manufactured with high confidence
labeled genuine viral events are not flagged manufactured
every verdict records its contributing signals
revisit_triggers: a new manufacturing tactic defeats the current signal set
verdict accuracy drops on the labeled audit set

nodes.definition: Apply the hard gate that genuine hype requires at least N independent origins after provenance deduplication and method-bias discounting; below N, even large adjusted hype is classified as not-genuine regardless of volume (scope finding FP7).
inputs: independent-origin count after dedup and discounting

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the independence threshold N or its discounting inputs are revised

pros.claim: A bright-line independence threshold operationalizes the scope finding: no amount of single-origin volume can be promoted to 'genuine'
pros.example: a 2M-view campaign from one independent origin fails the >=N gate

cons.claim: A fixed N is a blunt instrument; the right threshold varies by topic risk and platform, and a too-high N suppresses real niche trends
cons.example: a genuine small-community trend with few but real origins is gated out

failure_modes: setting N so high that real niche hype fails
letting adjusted volume override the independence gate
applying N before provenance dedup inflates the origin count
acceptance_tests: any signal set with fewer than N independent origins is classified not-genuine regardless of adjusted volume
known genuine multi-origin trends pass the gate on the labeled set
revisit_triggers: topic-risk policy changes the required N
real niche trends are systematically gated out

nodes.definition: Classify the topic's current trajectory as emerging, accelerating, plateauing, or fading using the position and slope on the fitted diffusion curve relative to its inflection point.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: trajectory-phase boundaries or slope thresholds change

pros.claim: Phase labels make the genuine-hype verdict actionable by saying not just whether but when and where on the curve
pros.example: 'accelerating with rising independent origins' is a buy signal; 'fading plateau' is not

cons.claim: Phase boundaries are fuzzy near the inflection point and a brief dip can be misread as fading
cons.example: a weekend lull on a still-growing topic is mislabeled fading

failure_modes: misreading a transient dip as fading
late inflection detection delays the accelerating label
phase assigned from noisy slope estimates
acceptance_tests: assigned phases match held-out trends' realized continuation on the labeled set
phase transitions are stable under short-window noise
revisit_triggers: slope-threshold policy changes
phase labels mismatch realized trend continuation

nodes.definition: Reconcile the five platform signals onto a common time base, audience normalization, and topic definition before independence accounting, so that origin counting compares like with like.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: platform set changes or topic-alignment/normalization rules are revised

pros.claim: Reconciling platforms first prevents spurious independence from mismatched topics or time windows masquerading as distinct origins
pros.example: aligning a hashtag and a search term to one topic avoids double-counting them as origins

cons.claim: Over-harmonization can merge genuinely different framings of a topic, hiding a real second origin
cons.example: two distinct but related stories forced into one topic lose a real independent origin

failure_modes: misaligned time windows fabricate or hide concurrency
audience normalization errors distort relative magnitudes
topic over-merging erases a real origin
acceptance_tests: the same artifact across platforms aligns to one topic and time window on the labeled set
distinct topics are not force-merged during reconciliation
revisit_triggers: the platform panel changes
topic-alignment errors surface in independence audits

nodes.definition: Govern the numeric policy parameters (anomaly significance level, bot-risk cutoffs, saturation weights, and the independence threshold N) as versioned, auditable settings with documented rationale and review cadence.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any governed parameter is changed or a new parameter is introduced

pros.claim: Treating N and thresholds as governed policy, not buried constants, keeps the genuine-vs-manufactured line auditable and contestable
pros.example: a threshold change is versioned with before/after impact on labeled cases

cons.claim: Heavy governance can ossify thresholds that need fast adaptation when adversaries shift tactics
cons.example: a quarterly review cadence lags a same-week manufacturing innovation

failure_modes: silent threshold edits with no audit trail
thresholds tuned to a single high-profile case
governance cadence too slow for adversarial drift
acceptance_tests: every threshold change is versioned with documented rationale and labeled-case impact
current parameter set reproduces the certified validation results
revisit_triggers: adversary tactics shift faster than the review cadence
a parameter change degrades labeled-case accuracy

nodes.definition: Maintain a per-verdict evidence ledger recording the baseline, anomaly score, origin count, discounts, structural virality, search corroboration, and the parameter version, so any genuine-vs-manufactured call is reproducible and contestable.
inputs: all upstream signals and the parameter version

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ledger schema changes or a new evidence field is added to verdicts

pros.claim: A reproducible evidence ledger turns a hype verdict into an auditable claim with provenance, essential when a manufactured-hype call is disputed
pros.example: a flagged campaign's ledger shows exactly which signals and N drove the call

cons.claim: Comprehensive ledgers add storage and write cost and can leak sensitive source-attribution detail if mishandled
cons.example: retaining full account-level evidence raises privacy and disclosure concerns

failure_modes: a verdict issued without a complete ledger entry
ledger omits the parameter version used
sensitive source detail over-retained
acceptance_tests: every issued verdict has a complete, parameter-stamped ledger entry
a ledger entry alone reproduces the verdict under its recorded parameters
revisit_triggers: ledger schema changes
a disputed verdict cannot be reproduced from its ledger

nodes.definition: Backtest the baseline and diffusion model against historical labeled organic and manufactured episodes to calibrate residual distributions and validate that anomaly and independence signals separate the two classes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the labeled backtest set or calibration window changes

pros.claim: Backtesting against labeled genuine and manufactured episodes turns the pipeline's thresholds into empirically calibrated, not guessed, settings
pros.example: replaying a known astroturf quarter sets the bot-risk cutoff where it actually separates classes

cons.claim: Backtests overfit to past tactics and labels are noisy, so calibrated thresholds can fail on novel manufacturing
cons.example: a threshold tuned on last year's farms misses a new account-aging tactic

failure_modes: overfitting thresholds to historical episodes
label noise in the backtest corrupts calibration
leakage from using test episodes in baseline fitting
acceptance_tests: on the held-out backtest split, genuine and manufactured episodes separate above the target margin
calibrated residual distributions match the held-out organic class
revisit_triggers: new manufacturing tactics appear in production
backtest separation degrades on refreshed labels

nodes.definition: Assemble the final decision report: the genuine-vs-manufactured verdict, the independent-origin count versus N, the adjusted-hype magnitude and trajectory, the driving evidence, and the confidence, for downstream consumers.
inputs: gate verdict, trajectory, ledger, and backtest context

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: report contract or downstream consumer requirements change

pros.claim: A single decision report with verdict, N-comparison, magnitude, trajectory, and confidence makes the analysis directly actionable and contestable
pros.example: a report reading 'genuine, 6>=N=4 origins, accelerating, high confidence' is decision-ready

cons.claim: Compressing a multi-signal analysis into one report can hide tail uncertainty unless the confidence and evidence are surfaced
cons.example: a confident-sounding verdict masks a borderline origin count

failure_modes: report omits the origin-count-vs-N margin
confidence not surfaced alongside the verdict
trajectory dropped, leaving timing ambiguous
acceptance_tests: every report states verdict, origin count vs N, adjusted hype, trajectory, and confidence
a consumer can reconstruct the call from the report and its linked ledger
revisit_triggers: report contract changes
consumers report the verdict was not actionable as delivered

edges.why_related: reconciled like-with-like signals feed the independence count so platforms are not double-counted as origins
absent search corroboration is evidence a hype event is push-manufactured
backtests recalibrate how much method correlation discounts independence
governed significance levels constrain what anomaly detection flags
governed bot-risk cutoffs constrain the adjusted-hype discount
backtest separation metrics drive governed threshold updates
the ledger supplies the evidence the report summarizes and links
broadcast-vs-viral structure informs whether a trajectory reflects genuine person-to-person spread
large adjusted volume from too-few independent origins conflicts with the genuine-hype independence requirement
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: independence dominates volume: when adjusted hype is large but independent origins are below N, the >=N gate fails the event regardless of magnitude (scope finding FP7)

edges.why_related: a drifting organic baseline conflicts with a fixed anomaly threshold, producing systematic false bursts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: recalibrate the baseline rather than the threshold when residuals drift: a platform algorithm change shifts 'normal', so refit ORGANIC_BASELINE before trusting anomaly flags

edges.why_related: aggressive provenance clustering and accurate independent-origin counting pull in opposite directions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: tune clustering to maximize independence-count accuracy on labeled data: under-clustering inflates origins, over-clustering hides real ones, so calibrate against known independent creations

edges.why_related: slow threshold governance conflicts with rapidly evolving manufacturing tactics the adjudicator must catch
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: favor adaptability under audit: when adversary tactics shift faster than the review cadence, allow expedited parameter updates with retroactive backtest validation rather than waiting for the cycle

conflict_axes.name: independence_count_vs_raw_volume
conflict_axes.description: Genuine hype is defined by independent origins, but raw volume is the loudest and most gameable signal; volume must never substitute for independence.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply the >=N independence gate before volume is allowed to influence the genuine verdict

conflict_axes.name: baseline_recalibration_vs_threshold_stability
conflict_axes.description: Algorithm changes drift the organic baseline, so a stable anomaly threshold yields false bursts; but constant recalibration undermines comparability.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: refit the baseline on drift and version the change; keep thresholds stable between certified baselines

conflict_axes.name: aggressive_clustering_vs_origin_preservation
conflict_axes.description: Collapsing reposts prevents inflated independence, but over-clustering merges genuinely distinct independent creations and erases real origins.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: calibrate clustering thresholds against labeled independent-creation cases

conflict_axes.name: single_signal_simplicity_vs_multi_signal_robustness
conflict_axes.description: One headline metric is easy to communicate but trivially gameable; multi-signal fusion is robust but harder to interpret and can be overconfident.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fuse multiple signals for the verdict but report a single confidence-bearing summary

conflict_axes.name: push_engagement_vs_pull_search_corroboration
conflict_axes.description: Platform engagement is push-inflatable while search interest is a harder-to-fake pull signal; disagreement is informative but search is coarse and laggy.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat search concordance as corroborating evidence, not a veto, given its coarseness and lag

conflict_axes.name: bot_recall_vs_grassroots_precision
conflict_axes.description: Aggressive bot detection catches more inauthentic engagement but risks suppressing genuine grassroots accounts as false positives.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tune bot-risk cutoffs to bound grassroots false positives on labeled organic cases

conflict_axes.name: broadcast_reach_vs_structural_virality
conflict_axes.description: High reach from a single broadcaster looks like virality but lacks the multi-generational structure of genuine person-to-person spread.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: weight structural virality, not reach alone, when judging genuine grassroots spread

conflict_axes.name: saturation_discount_vs_late_genuine_demand
conflict_axes.description: Discounting plateau-phase engagement as recycled attention can wrongly penalize a genuine second wave of real new demand.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: distinguish a fitted-curve plateau from a fresh independent-origin second wave before discounting

conflict_axes.name: governance_cadence_vs_adversary_adaptation
conflict_axes.description: Versioned, slow threshold governance preserves auditability but lags adversaries who change tactics within a review cycle.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allow expedited, retroactively backtested parameter changes for confirmed adversary shifts

edge_cases.description: Five platforms all amplify one press release, creating apparent cross-platform consensus that is actually a single origin.
edge_cases.trigger: correlated platform echoes counted as independent before provenance dedup
edge_cases.mitigation: cluster to the seed and collapse correlated platforms to one independent origin before counting

edge_cases.description: A 2M-view campaign originates from a single independent origin yet has enormous adjusted hype.
edge_cases.trigger: large adjusted volume from fewer than N independent origins
edge_cases.mitigation: fail the >=N independence gate regardless of volume per scope finding FP7

edge_cases.description: A platform algorithm change doubles organic reach, so a stable anomaly threshold flags normal engagement as bursts.
edge_cases.trigger: anomaly threshold applied against a drifted, stale organic baseline
edge_cases.mitigation: refit and version the baseline on detected drift before trusting anomaly flags

edge_cases.description: An astroturf network of aged, warmed accounts evades behavioral bot detection and looks grassroots.
edge_cases.trigger: bot detector blind to a new account-aging evasion tactic
edge_cases.mitigation: corroborate with independence, structural virality, and search; escalate to backtest recalibration

edge_cases.description: Two creators independently film the same public event and perceptual hashing merges them into one seed.
edge_cases.trigger: over-aggressive provenance clustering merges genuinely distinct creations
edge_cases.mitigation: calibrate clustering against labeled independent-creation cases to preserve real origins

edge_cases.description: A star-shaped broadcast from one influencer reaches millions and is mistaken for grassroots virality.
edge_cases.trigger: reach used as a virality proxy without structural-virality measurement
edge_cases.mitigation: compute the Wiener-index structural virality and label broadcasts as non-grassroots

edge_cases.description: Two 'independent' trackers both purchase the same third-party data panel, faking corroboration.
edge_cases.trigger: common-method bias from a shared data pipeline not discounted
edge_cases.mitigation: identify shared panels and discount method-correlated sources from the independence count

edge_cases.description: A paid search campaign lifts the trends curve so search interest falsely corroborates a push event.
edge_cases.trigger: search interest treated as a clean pull signal despite ad-driven query inflation
edge_cases.mitigation: treat search as corroborating not decisive and watch for ad-spend-driven query spikes

edge_cases.description: A genuine niche-community trend has few but real independent origins and is gated out by a too-high N.
edge_cases.trigger: independence threshold N set too high for niche topics
edge_cases.mitigation: govern N by topic risk and review niche false-negatives in backtests

edge_cases.description: A genuine second wave of new demand on a near-saturated topic is wrongly discounted as recycled attention.
edge_cases.trigger: saturation discount applied without checking for fresh independent origins
edge_cases.mitigation: check for new independent origins before applying the plateau saturation discount

edge_cases.description: A manufactured-hype verdict is disputed and cannot be reproduced because the parameter version was not recorded.
edge_cases.trigger: verdict issued without a complete, parameter-stamped evidence ledger
edge_cases.mitigation: stamp every verdict with its parameter version and full driving evidence in the ledger

edge_cases.description: Adversary tactics shift within a single review cycle and the governed thresholds lag, letting a campaign pass.
edge_cases.trigger: governance cadence slower than adversary adaptation
edge_cases.mitigation: allow expedited retroactively backtested parameter updates for confirmed tactic shifts

workflow.description: Estimate expected engagement per platform/region/category and its confidence intervals as the deviation reference.
workflow.gate: baseline reproduces held-out organic items within its interval

workflow.description: Fit Bass p/q/m to cumulative adoption to characterize the expected genuine adoption S-curve.
workflow.gate: p and q lie in plausible platform ranges; tail reproduced within tolerance

workflow.description: Align the five platform signals to a common time base, audience normalization, and topic definition.
workflow.gate: the same artifact across platforms aligns to one topic and window

workflow.description: Flag bursts where observed engagement exceeds baseline and curve expectations beyond the governed significance level.
workflow.gate: false-positive rate under target on labeled organic surges

workflow.description: Collapse cross-posts, screenshots, and re-uploads to single provenance seeds.
workflow.gate: known repost chains collapse to one seed each

workflow.description: Reduce signals to distinct independent origins and discount common-method correlation.
workflow.gate: correlated platforms and shared-method sources collapse to true origins

workflow.description: Discount raw engagement by bot risk and audience saturation to adjusted hype with an interval.
workflow.gate: manufactured campaigns fall far below raw; genuine stay close

workflow.description: Reconstruct the cascade tree and compute structural virality to separate broadcast from grassroots spread.
workflow.gate: broadcasts score low and grassroots cascades score high

workflow.description: Fuse anomaly, independence, bot, structural, and search signals into a manufactured-vs-genuine verdict.
workflow.gate: labeled astroturf adjudicated manufactured; genuine not flagged

workflow.description: Apply the >=N independent-origin gate; below N the event is not-genuine regardless of volume.
workflow.gate: fewer than N independent origins fails the gate regardless of adjusted volume

workflow.description: Label the trajectory emerging, accelerating, plateauing, or fading from curve position and slope.
workflow.gate: assigned phase matches realized continuation on labeled trends

workflow.description: Assemble the verdict, origin count vs N, adjusted hype, trajectory, evidence, and confidence into the decision report.
workflow.gate: report states verdict, origin-vs-N margin, magnitude, trajectory, and confidence

priority_rationale: ORGANIC_BASELINE and DIFFUSION_CURVE are foundational references; ANOMALY_DETECTION, PROVENANCE_CLUSTERING, and SOURCE_INDEPENDENCE establish deviation and independence; MANUFACTURED_HYPE and the >=N GENUINE_HYPE_THRESHOLD gate are the adjudication core; governance, ledger, backtest, and report close the method.

dominance_rules.rule: ORGANIC_BASELINE must be current (refit after any algorithm change) before ANOMALY_DETECTION flags are trusted
dominance_rules.rationale: a drifted baseline makes every anomaly score systematically wrong
dominance_rules.trigger: anomaly detection runs against a baseline older than the last algorithm change
dominance_rules.action: block anomaly flags until the baseline is refit and versioned

dominance_rules.rule: PROVENANCE_CLUSTERING must run before SOURCE_INDEPENDENCE counts origins
dominance_rules.rationale: counting origins before collapsing reposts inflates apparent independence
dominance_rules.trigger: independent-origin counting requested on unclustered signals
dominance_rules.action: block counting until provenance clusters are assigned

dominance_rules.rule: The GENUINE_HYPE_THRESHOLD >=N independence gate dominates raw and adjusted volume
dominance_rules.rationale: scope finding FP7: no amount of single-origin volume can be promoted to genuine
dominance_rules.trigger: a verdict would label an event genuine with fewer than N independent origins
dominance_rules.action: fail the gate regardless of volume and record the margin

dominance_rules.rule: COMMON_METHOD_BIAS discounting must be applied before the independence count feeds the threshold
dominance_rules.rationale: shared-method sources are not independent and would inflate the origin count
dominance_rules.trigger: origin count reaches the threshold without method-bias discounting
dominance_rules.action: apply method-correlation discount before evaluating the gate

dominance_rules.rule: MANUFACTURED_HYPE verdicts must record which signals drove them in the EVIDENCE_LEDGER
dominance_rules.rationale: an unrecorded verdict is not reproducible or contestable
dominance_rules.trigger: a verdict is issued without a ledger entry
dominance_rules.action: block issuance until the evidence ledger entry is complete

dominance_rules.rule: BOT_RISK_SCORING cutoffs must be governed, not ad hoc, before discounting raw hype
dominance_rules.rationale: ungoverned cutoffs make adjusted hype non-comparable and gameable
dominance_rules.trigger: a bot-risk cutoff is changed outside THRESHOLD_GOVERNANCE
dominance_rules.action: route the change through governed, versioned parameters

dominance_rules.rule: STRUCTURAL_VIRALITY must be considered before reach is treated as grassroots virality
dominance_rules.rationale: a broadcast and true virality can have identical reach
dominance_rules.trigger: a high-reach broadcast is labeled grassroots without structural measurement
dominance_rules.action: compute structural virality and re-label broadcasts as non-grassroots

dominance_rules.rule: SATURATION_ESTIMATE must check for fresh independent origins before discounting plateau engagement
dominance_rules.rationale: a genuine second wave of new demand should not be discounted as recycled attention
dominance_rules.trigger: plateau saturation discount applied while new independent origins are appearing
dominance_rules.action: defer the saturation discount when new independent origins are present

dominance_rules.rule: THRESHOLD_GOVERNANCE must version every parameter change with labeled-case impact before it takes effect
dominance_rules.rationale: silent threshold edits make the genuine-vs-manufactured line unauditable
dominance_rules.trigger: a governed parameter changes without a versioned rationale and impact record
dominance_rules.action: block the change until it is versioned with rationale and backtest impact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not run anomaly detection on a stale baseline; refitting after a flagged-burst false alarm wastes the whole review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-reviewing a batch of false bursts caused by an un-refit baseline

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not count independent origins before provenance clustering; un-collapsing inflated origins later means redoing the verdict
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-adjudicating a campaign after discovering its origins were correlated echoes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not let adjusted volume override the >=N independence gate; reversing a wrongly-genuine verdict is costly and public
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retracting a 'genuine' label on a single-origin high-volume campaign

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip common-method discounting before the gate; an inflated origin count that passes must be re-litigated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-running the gate after discovering shared-panel non-independence

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not issue a verdict without a parameter-stamped ledger entry; reconstructing evidence for a dispute is expensive
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing a disputed verdict's evidence after the parameters changed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not treat reach as virality without structural measurement; relabeling a broadcast later invalidates downstream reports
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reissuing reports after a broadcast was misclassified as grassroots

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not change governed thresholds without versioning and backtest impact; untraceable edits force a full re-certification
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-certifying the whole pipeline after an untraceable threshold edit

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not over-cluster provenance to inflate dedup; recovering wrongly-merged real origins requires re-running clustering and counting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-deriving independence after distinct creations were merged into one seed

iteration_protocol.trigger: anomaly false-positive rate exceeds target on review
iteration_protocol.action: refit and re-version ORGANIC_BASELINE and re-tune the significance level in ANOMALY_DETECTION via THRESHOLD_GOVERNANCE

iteration_protocol.trigger: a campaign passes as genuine but is later confirmed manufactured
iteration_protocol.action: audit SOURCE_INDEPENDENCE and COMMON_METHOD_BIAS for missed correlation and recalibrate in BASELINE_BACKTEST

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-volume single-origin event is wrongly labeled genuine
iteration_protocol.action: verify the >=N gate in GENUINE_HYPE_THRESHOLD dominates RAW_VS_ADJUSTED_HYPE volume

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new bot or account-aging evasion tactic is observed
iteration_protocol.action: update BOT_RISK_SCORING heuristics and recalibrate cutoffs through THRESHOLD_GOVERNANCE and BASELINE_BACKTEST

iteration_protocol.trigger: genuine niche trends are systematically gated out
iteration_protocol.action: review the topic-risk-conditioned N in GENUINE_HYPE_THRESHOLD and THRESHOLD_GOVERNANCE against niche backtest false-negatives

iteration_protocol.trigger: provenance clustering merges distinct independent creations
iteration_protocol.action: recalibrate clustering thresholds in PROVENANCE_CLUSTERING against labeled independent-creation cases and re-check SOURCE_INDEPENDENCE

iteration_protocol.trigger: a verdict is disputed and cannot be reproduced
iteration_protocol.action: audit EVIDENCE_LEDGER completeness and parameter stamping and patch DECISION_REPORT to surface the ledger link

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
